# SignalBridge AI

> SignalBridge AI is a local-first, zero-knowledge orchestrator connecting private Signal messaging with custom local AI agents, LLM backends (Ollama, vLLM, Llama.cpp, DeepSeek), and automated workflows.

## Overview
- **Product Name**: SignalBridge AI
- **Developer / Publisher**: Tech Pro / Zoth Studio Team
- **Website**: https://signalbridge-ai.757tech.pro/
- **Portfolio Showcase**: https://nullai.tech/
- **Encryption**: Signal Protocol End-to-End Encryption (X3DH + Double Ratchet)
- **Primary Purpose**: Provide secure mobile access to home-server or self-hosted AI models via Signal protocol without routing unencrypted payloads through cloud intermediaries.

## Key Technical Features
1. **Signal Protocol Native**: Operates natively inside Signal's double ratchet end-to-end encryption scheme.
2. **Zero-Knowledge Architecture**: Message contents and private keys never leave local hardware.
3. **Multi-Model Support**: Direct routing to Ollama (Llama 3.3, DeepSeek R1), LangChain agents, vLLM, and custom REST/WebSocket webhooks.
4. **Interactive CLI & Telemetry**: Built-in signal routing console, encrypted packet inspection, and fallback simulation engine.
5. **API & Webhook Gateway**: RESTful endpoints and WebSocket streams for real-time agent responses.

## Quick Start Setup (HowTo)
1. Install `signalbridge-cli` via npm or download release binary.
2. Link your local Signal phone number using `signalbridge register --phone="+1..."`.
3. Configure your local AI backends in `config.yaml` (e.g. `http://localhost:11434` for Ollama).
4. Run `signalbridge start` to initialize the secure local daemon bridge.
5. Send messages to your bot contact on Signal to interact with your local agents!

## Frequently Asked Questions
- **Does SignalBridge host user data?** No. All encryption and model inference happen locally or on private user infrastructure.
- **Can I connect open-source models like Llama 3 or DeepSeek R1?** Yes, SignalBridge supports Ollama, vLLM, LocalAI, and any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint.
- **How does authentication work?** Identity keys are verified via the standard Signal protocol prekey exchange.
